metadata.title: Claude, Campaign Plan.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude invents a bespoke marketing strategy or fills in a fixed spec, using the campaign-plan skill's own task and trigger rule as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that the skill doesn't make Claude a strategist -- it makes Claude fill six fixed slots, the same way, only when the words match its triggers.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 ('plan a launch campaign for a new fitness app' run through the same three-step pipeline, then run again unchanged; contrasted with a non-matching request that never starts it)

beats.narration_text: You ask Claude for a campaign plan, and it's tempting to picture it inventing a strategy from nothing. It doesn't -- it assembles one, from a fixed set of written steps. What's actually in that file?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'You ask for a campaign plan. Claude must invent the whole strategy, right?', hesitates on 'invent', corrects to 'assemble'

props.text:
You ask for a campaign plan.
Claude must invent
the whole strategy,
right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('invent' -> 'assemble') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: It's a fair guess -- Claude can talk marketing strategy in general. But ask it for a campaign plan twice, for two completely different products, and the same six pieces come back every time: objectives, audience, messaging, channel strategy, a content calendar, and success metrics. That's not improvisation. That's a spec being filled in.

shot.new_visual_element: Two different product requests produce the identical six-piece shape, side by side

production_viz.label: Same six pieces, different products
production_viz.mechanic: Two request cards draw in side by side -- 'fitness app' and 'coffee subscription'. Beneath each, the same six labeled slots fill in, in the same order and the same shape: objectives, audience, messaging, channel strategy, content calendar, success metrics. The two shapes are identical even though the products are not.

beats.narration_text: The fix is one file: SKILL.md. It's the whole instruction set -- one page telling Claude to produce exactly those six pieces, and naming exactly when to fire: a product launch, a lead-generation push, an awareness campaign, or a request for a week-by-week content calendar. Say 'plan a launch campaign for a new fitness app,' and it matches, reads the file top to bottom, and executes each step in order.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- 'plan a launch campaign for a new fitness app' matched against the trigger list, then walked through Read, Execute, Return

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- matched, then walked step by step
production_viz.mechanic: A SKILL.md card sits at top with a short list of trigger phrases beneath it: 'product launch', 'lead-gen push', 'awareness campaign', 'content calendar'. THE ANCHOR. The words 'plan a launch campaign for a new fitness app' type themselves out below, a bracket snaps to the matching trigger phrase, and the query flows left to right through three labelled stations -- READ, EXECUTE, RETURN -- lighting each in turn. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Ask that same thing again next month, and Claude walks the same file, in the same order -- the six pieces come back again. That's the payoff of a written spec: repeatable, not reinvented. But ask something the file never named -- say, 'write one tweet for this product' -- and the trigger never matches. The pipeline doesn't start; you get whatever Claude would say without the skill at all.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the same query run again, identical steps; then a non-matching request that never enters the pipeline

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- same steps again, then nothing starts
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 SEQUENCE RETURNS, identical: 'plan a launch campaign for a new fitness app' flows through READ, EXECUTE, RETURN again, same lighted path. Beside it, a different, unmatched request types itself out -- 'write one tweet for this product' -- no bracket snaps to any trigger, and the three stations stay dark. A line of small italic text appears beneath: 'no match. no pipeline. just Claude, on its own.'

beats.narration_text: campaign-plan doesn't make Claude a strategist. It makes Claude fill six fixed slots, the same way, every time your words match what the file was built to hear.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. I want a campaign plan for a product I'm describing to you now. Read the campaign-plan skill and walk me through what you'll do, step by step, before you do it. Watch for two things: does Claude name the six pieces before writing them, and does it match your request to one of its own stated triggers? Liam, in for Bear.
